A [[geodesic]] [[metric space]] <math>X</math> is called a '''''tree-graded space''''' with respect to a collection of [[Connected space|connected]] proper subsets called ''pieces'', if any two distinct pieces [[Intersection (set theory)|intersect]] in at most one point, and every non-trivial simple [[geodesic]] [[triangle]] of <math>X</math> is contained in one of the pieces.

Tree-graded spaces behave like [[real tree]]s "up to what can happen within the pieces", while allowing non-tree-like behavior within the pieces. For example, any [[Topological embedding|topologically embedded]] circle is contained in a piece; there is a well-defined [[Projections onto convex sets|projection]] on every piece, such that every [[path-connected]] subset meeting a piece in at most one point projects to a unique point on that piece; the space is naturally [[Fibration|fibered]] into real trees that are [[Transversality (mathematics)|transverse]] to pieces; and pieces can be "merged along embedded paths" in a way that preserves a tree-graded structure.

Tree-graded spaces were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last1 = Druţu | first1 = Cornelia | author1-link = Cornelia Druţu
 | last2 = Sapir | first2 = Mark |author2-link= Mark Sapir|year=2005}} in their study of the [[Ultralimit#Asymptotic cones|asymptotic cones]] of [[hyperbolic group|relatively hyperbolic group]]s. This point of view allows for a notion of relative hyperbolicity that makes sense for [[geodesic metric space]]s and which is invariant under [[Quasi-isometry|quasi-isometries]].

For instance, a [[CAT(0) group]] has [[CAT(0) group with isolated flats|isolated flats]], if and only if all its asymptotic cones are tree-graded metric spaces all of whose pieces are isometric to [[euclidean space]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hruska |first=G. Christopher |last2=Kleiner |first2=Bruce |date=2005-08-08 |title=Hadamard spaces with isolated flats, with an appendix written jointly with Mohamad Hindawi |url=https://msp.org/gt/2005/9-3/p08.xhtml |journal=Geometry & Topology |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=1501–1538 |doi=10.2140/gt.2005.9.1501 |issn=1364-0380|arxiv=math/0411232 }}</ref>
